questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience the Italian culture with its beautiful architecture, good food and lots of sun, which is why I chose an exchange program in Rome

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, I think it was fairly easy. However, I don't think you can avoid the fact that finding information can be confusing at first, as you have to get used to new learning portals etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Prior to the start of classes, an orientation evening was held at Luiss, where we were introduced to the university and given all the important information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult to find housing, so I would recommend starting in good time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: it's nice, and either way it is not possible to live at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy to register for courses. However, I found it challenging that exam schedules were not published until mid-October, which meant that your exams could be very close and potentially on the same day.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember the exact registration process, but I don't remember it as being difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a mobility office at Luiss that you could email or call.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to check the class schedule for all the classes you want to register for in order to avoid time schedule clashes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the academic level varied a bit from course to course, but overall I found it easier compared to KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more class teaching than classic lectures, with student presentations and in-class debates.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Politics, Comparative History of Political Systems, Crisis Communication, Sociology of Terrorism and The International Relation of Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Comparative History of Politcal Systems with Rosario Forlenza

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not have any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Coffee is cheap and in general you can eat out for much less compared to Denmark. Also a card for all the public transportation in Rome is only 35 euro a month. 
The housing was more expensive than what I expected, but I also know someone who had a lower monthly rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a football tournament for exchange students that spanned the entire semester. There were also parties, sports days and weekend trips out of Rome, but I didn't take part in any of these.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The football tournament

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a weekend trip to Napoli and Firenze. It is easy to get there by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything is just a little more chaotic in Rome compared to Denmark, and public transportation can especially be challenging as you can never count on the time schedule.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture and that there is so much life in the streets all year round, with people drinking coffee in cafes and eating in restaurants. I also appreciated the warm weather, with the sun shining almost every day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything right now

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a new city and culture, and then all the people I met during my stay in Rome

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That it ended

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
